title: Decomposing High-Frequency Order Flow: Commonality and Idiosyncratic Trade Imbalance
abstract: Standard measures of trade imbalance often fail to distinguish between asset-specific directional pressure and market-wide trading activity, leading to misleading inferences. This paper develops a continuous-time framework to decompose high-frequency order flow into common and idiosyncratic components using bivariate Cox processes with a latent common factor. We propose a novel Idiosyncratic Trade Imbalance (IdTI) index, designed to filter out interference from common factors. To facilitate inference, we establish a coupling result using a fixed number of observations that supports Poisson approximations for high-frequency data and develop a Bayesian procedure with asymptotic validity. Simulation results indicate that traditional frequentist methods become unreliable during market-wide intensity shocks, while our proposed methodology maintains robust coverage. Applying the framework to tick-by-tick data during major product launches and FOMC announcements, we find that the idiosyncratic measure unmasks significant directional convictions that are otherwise obscured by common trade intensity.
